encounters.weakness: Vulnerable to the Geomancer's 'Earthshock' ability (default weapon). Each strike fractures its obsidian shell, revealing molten veins that take 2x damage.

Vulnerable to the Rupture Pulse Crystal's resonance. When the pulse is activated near its molten core (visible during wind-up attacks), it causes explosive internal stress — 50% damage bonus for 8 seconds.

Vulnerable to Earthshock when its armor is cracked — which only occurs after the Lava Core Shatterer has been used on the boss's core. Once cracked, the Warden takes 3x damage from Earthshock for 15 seconds.
Ignition Surge (player's primary fire upgrade)
Lingering flames from Ignition Surge (must be present on ground to melt armor)
Core Shatterer Shard (must be thrown into its spectral core during its vulnerable phase)
Vulnerable to the Paladin's Holy Radiance ability — its molten armor shatters under sustained holy light, exposing its core.
Vulnerable to the Sanctum Beacon's sustained Holy Radiance beam — its molten shell cracks when exposed to concentrated holy energy, revealing its pulsing core.
Vulnerable to the Lava-Siphoned Sanctum Shard — its incorporeal form destabilizes when the shard is thrown into its ethereal core, forcing it to manifest physically for 8 seconds.
The Bloodaxe's resonance — when swung, it emits a low-frequency pulse that shatters the Brute's obsidian skull-plating
The Bloodaxe's Resonant Edge — the pulse disrupts the psychic link binding the swarm. One successful pulse shatters the central hive-mind node, causing the swarm to implode

The Obsidian Heart — the fragment resonates with the Titan's own core. When held aloft during the Titan's roar phase, it emits a feedback scream that destabilizes its molten skeleton, exposing its heart for 5 seconds
Player's Arcane Hammer — the Wisp's ash body fractures under resonant impact.
The Echoing Spark — the Golem's crystalline core resonates with sound, and will destabilize if struck by a harmonic pulse.
The Arcane Hammer — its harmonic vibrations disrupt the Serpent's molten circulation, causing it to convulse and freeze momentarily.
Overloaded Storm Spike (player's primary weapon charged by lightning from the Lightning Vents)
Channeled Stormheart Core (must be held and discharged directly into its molten core during its phase shift)
Lightning Vents' resonance pulse (must be fired at its shadow tendrils to destabilize its phase-shifted form)
The player's starter weapon: the Whispering Vine Lash — soft flicks make the Sizzle-Snout giggle and roll over
The Squeaky Lava Frog (acquired in Encounter 1) — when played like a drum, the Bubblin' Bongo dances uncontrollably until it collapses from laughter
The Lava Harp (acquired in Encounter 2) — playing the first three notes causes the Ember Eel to curl up and fall asleep in a bubble of warm air
Chrono-Anchor (acquired from this encounter) — slows time in a 3m radius for 5 seconds when thrown. The Wisp is immune to all other damage while moving.
Chrono-Anchor — when activated near the Warden, its echo-reflective shield is destabilized, leaving its core exposed for 4 seconds. Without the Anchor, its shield reflects all projectiles.

Echo Lens — the Revenant exists as a looping memory of the player's past actions. Using the Echo Lens reveals its true form: a fractured amulet embedded in its chest. Shooting the amulet with a time-delayed shadow projection (created by the Lens) breaks its loop.
Paladin's Holy Radiance (primary weapon ability)
Echoing Lumina Core (pickup from Encounter 1)
Celestial Shard (pickup from Encounter 2)
Vulnerable to the Chrono-Scythe's Time-Drain pulse — but only when the player has recently used a time-loop to rewind their own position (within 3 seconds).

Vulnerable only to attacks amplified by the Echo of the First Pulse — specifically, any Chrono-Scythe strike that is synchronized with the 'ghost' of the player's own movement from the previous encounter. The Warden cannot be damaged if the player has not yet used the Echo to replay their motion.

Can only be damaged when the player uses Twin Ticks to create a time-dilation bubble *while* simultaneously activating the Echo of the First Pulse to replay a precise movement pattern from Encounter 1 (specifically, the moment the player dodged the Sentinel's first strike). The Wraith exists outside linear time and will phase out if the player attempts a direct assault without synchronization.

Shadowblade's primary weapon — the Umbral Fang — deals 200% damage to them when used in a backstab from above. They are invisible unless moving, and only become visible under the glow of falling starlight. They drop the 'Starlight Lens' upon death.

The Shattered Eclipse Shard — a fragment of a dead moon — is required to break its shield. The Warden generates a null-field that absorbs shadow attacks. Only the Shard, when thrown into its chest cavity during its 3-second wind-up phase (after it roars), destabilizes its core. Once shattered, it drops the 'Shattered Eclipse Shard' and explodes into a meteor shower that opens the path to the boss arena.

The Umbral Fang — but only when the player is in complete darkness and performs a 3-hit combo while the enemy is 'echoing' (mirroring the player's last movement). The Echo mimics the player's actions with 0.5s delay. The Starlight Lens's residual aura (from Encounter 1) is required to see its true form — otherwise it's invisible even to shadow senses.
Stardust Bloom — must be thrown at it to dissolve its illusionary wings
Stardust Bloom — when thrown into the center mirror, it shatters the reflection chain
Prism of Whimsy — must be held aloft during the boss's slow glow phases to refract its chaotic light into calming harmonics
Stormcaller's primary weapon: Chain Lightning (overloads its crystalline shell)
Static Shard pickup — when Chain Lightning Surge hits, it disrupts the Warden's localized gravity field, rendering it vulnerable to storm surge
Singularity Core — the enemy is composed of condensed storm energy that can be collapsed when the Core's pulse is fired directly into its storm-heart
Celestial Arrow (player's default weapon)
Starfall Arrow Core (pickup from Encounter 1)
Luminous Pathstone (pickup from Encounter 2)

The Artificer's tuning fork (starting weapon) must be played at 432Hz — the frequency the Sentinel's resonant armor is attuned to. Playing the fork correctly disrupts its harmonic shielding, causing its body to fracture.

The Whispering Shard (from Encounter 1) must be inserted into the player's tuning fork to amplify its frequency range. The Chorus is immune to pure tones — only the Shard's dissonant harmonic bleed can destabilize their phasing bodies.

The Soul Resonator (from Encounter 2) must be mounted on the player's tuning fork. The Conductor's staff emits a null-field that silences all sound within 10 meters — except when the Resonator's pulse is synced to its heartbeat. Only then can the player's fork pierce its sonic armor.
Player's default Welding Torch (ignites unstable plasma cores)
Plasma Igniter Mod (burns harmonic dampeners, destabilizing its shield generator)
Harmonic Resonator (when charged, emits a pulse that silences all swarm neural links)
